articleTitle: On Cusp form Coefficients in Exponential Sums
A Stone–weierstrass Theorem for Postliminal JB‐Algebras
abstract: We prove the strong Stone–Weierstrass conjecture for postliminal JB‐algebras: if B is a JB‐subalgebra of a postliminal JB‐algebra A such that B separates P(A) ∪ {0}, then B = A.

articleTitle: Stable phantom maps between classifying spaces of compact lie groups
abstract: Let G and H be compact Lie groups with classifying spaces BG and BH. In this note we determine the graded group of stable phantom maps between BG and BH.

articleTitle: The Euclidean Representations of the Fibonacci Groups
Permutation Involvement and Groups
abstract: Sets of permutations which are closed under both pattern involvement and multiplication are classified.

articleTitle: Unilaterally Invertible Normals are Invertible
abstract: The result stated in the title is a fundamental result about Banach algebras which appears to have escaped notice up to now.

articleTitle: Norm Preserving Extensions in JBW‐Triple Preduals
Diophantine Equations for Second‐Order Recursive Sequences of Polynomials
abstract: Let B be a non‐zero integer. Define the sequence of polynomials <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>G(x) by G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>(x) = 0, G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>(x) = 1, G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n+1</inf>(x) = <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>xG(x) + BG<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n−1</inf>(x), n ∈ N. We prove that the diophantine equation <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>G(x) = <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>G(y) for m, n ≥ 3, m ≠ n, has only finitely many solutions.

articleTitle: Geometric Monodromy and the Hyperbolic Disc
abstract: Symplectic four‐manifolds give rise to Lefschetz fibrations, which are determined by monodromy representations of free groups in mapping class groups. We study the topology of Lefschetz fibrations by analysing the action of the monodromy on the universal cover of a smooth fibre and give a new and simple proof that Lefschetz fibrations arising from Donaldson's construction via pencils of sections never decompose as non‐trivial fibre sums; in particular not all Lefschetz fibrations are fibre sums of holomorphic Lefschetz fibrations. We also show that there can never be isotopy classes of simple closed curve invariant under the monodromy and as a corollary we give a symplectic analogue of Manin's theorem, showing that Lefschetz fibrations admit at most finitely many homotopy classes of geometric section.

articleTitle: A Note on the Sum of a Prime and a Polynomial
abstract: We prove that ‘almost all’ positive integers can be represented as a sum of a prime and a value of a polynomial f ∈ Z[x], provided that f satisfies a necessary arithmetical condition.

articleTitle: A Class of Automorphism Groups of Polygonal Complexes
abstract: In this paper we construct a class of groups together with their actions on certain spaces called polygonal complexes. We give a complete description of the class of all groups which act by automorphisms simply transitively on the oriented edges of non‐positively curved polygonal complexes. This family of group actions is very natural from a geometrical viewpoint, being a kind of higher‐dimensional analogue of the actions of groups on their Cayley graphs (which are simply transitive on vertices). The construction is based on the notion of a non‐positively curved orbihedron and its fundamental group and generalizes the ideas of Ballmann and the author [2].

articleTitle: On the Symmetric Algebra of Stable Vector Bundles on Curves
abstract: Let X be a smooth projective curve of genus g ≥ 2 and E a general stable vector bundle on X with rank(E) = r and deg(E) = d > 0. Let z be the smallest integer with zd > 2gr. Here we study the graded algebra H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> (X, Sym(E)) := ⌖<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>≥<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> (X, S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> (E)) and prove that it is generated by elements of degree ≤ z.

articleTitle: Isoperimetric functions of nilpotent groups amalgamated along a cyclic subgroup
abstract: We show that amalgams of finitely generated torsionfree nilpotent groups of class≤c along a cyclic subgroup satisfy a polynomial isoperimetric inequality of degree at most 4c<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The distortion of the amalgamated subgroup is bounded above by a polynomial of degree c. We also give an example of a non‐cyclic amalgam of finitely generated torsionfree nilpotent groups along an abelian, isolated and normal subgroup having an exponential isoperimetric inequality.

articleTitle: Representation Type of the Blocks of Category Ο
abstract: In this paper the authors classify the blocks of the Category Ο for complex semisimple Lie algebras having finite, tame or wild representation type.

articleTitle: The Structure of the Discriminant of Some Space‐Curve Singularities
abstract: Among the space‐curve singularities of the simplest type are the so called wedges D = C ∨ L, consisting of a plane‐curve singularity C together with a line L transverse to the plane of C. In this note we describe the discriminant of D in terms of C. In particular, we show that the complement of the discriminant of D is a K(π, 1) if the complement of the discriminant of C is a K(π, 1). We also give a formula for the multiplicity of the discriminant of C ∨ L.

articleTitle: Arens regularity and the second dual of certain quotients of the fourier algebra
abstract: We show that every metrizable locally compact abelian group contains a closed subset E such that the restriction A(E) of the Fourier algebra to E is Arens regular whatever the bounded multiplication it is given, but such that neither Ã(E) nor A(E)** is Arens regular (in their natural multiplications).

articleTitle: On Subspaces of c0 and Extension of Operators into C(K)‐Spaces
abstract: Johnson and Zippin recently showed that if X is a weak<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>‐closed subspace of ℓ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and T : X → C(K) is any bounded operator then T can be extended to a bounded operator T̃ : ℓ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> → C(K). We give a converse result: ifX is a subspace of ℓ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> such that ℓ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>/X has an unconditional finite‐dimensional decomposition (UFDD) and every operator T : X → C(K) can be extended to ℓ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> then there is an automorphism τ of ℓ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> such that τ(X) is weak<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>‐closed. This result is proved by studying subspaces of c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> and several different characterizations of such subspaces are given.

articleTitle: Une estimation uniforme pour les intégrales simples à phase stationnaire
abstract: Nous apportons des précisions au lemme de la phase stationnaire concernant les intégrales oscillantes en dimension 1, prolongeant ainsi un résultat de Huxley (Glasgow Math. J. 36 (1994)). Nous appliquons ensuite notre résultat aux moyennes d'intégrales oscillantes lorsque la phase dépend régulièrement d'un paramètre, en prévision d'un article ultérieur sur les sommes d'exponentielles (en préparation).

articleTitle: Finitely presented subgroups of a product of two free groups
abstract: We use van Kampen diagram techniques to give a new geometric proof of the Baumslag and Roseblade result that a non‐free finitely presented subgroup of a direct product of two free groups is virtually a product of subgroups of the factors.

articleTitle: An Alternative Dunford–Pettis Property for JB‐Triples
abstract: We study a property weaker than the Dunford–Pettis property, introduced by Freedman, in the case of a JB<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>‐triple. It is shown that a JBW<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>‐triple W has this property if, and only if, W is a Hilbert space (regarded as a type 1 or 4 Cartan factor) or W has the Dunford–Pettis property. As a consequence, we get that the JBW<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>‐triples satisfying the Kadec–Klee property are finite‐dimensional or Hilbert spaces (regarded as Cartan factor 1 or 4).

articleTitle: Notes on Ideals of Roe Algebras
abstract: In this note we characterize some properties of ideals of Roe algebras, concerning order structure, minimal ideals, countably generated ideals, σ‐unit, etc.

articleTitle: Morita Equivalence for C‐Algebras with the Weak Banach–Saks Property
abstract: Let two C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>‐algebras A and B be Morita equivalent and let X be an A‐B‐imprimitivity bimodule. Consider the following conditions: (1) A has the weak Banach–Saks property; (2) B has the weak Banach–Saks property; (3) X has the uniform weak Banach–Saks property. Then we show that (1) and (2) are equivalent and (2) implies (3), and that if A or B is unital, then conditions (1) to (3) are equivalent.

articleTitle: Heat Kernel Estimates with Application to Compactness of Manifolds
abstract: Li and Yau type two‐sided heat kernel bounds are obtained for symmetric diffusions under a curvature–dimension condition, where the heat kernel upper bound is established for a more general case. As an application, the compactness of manifolds is studied using heat kernels. In particular, a conjecture by Bueler is proved.

articleTitle: Mixed Automorphic forms and Whittaker Vectors
abstract: We discuss Whittaker vectors and Jacquet integrals associated with mixed automorphic forms on real reductive groups and construct an analogue of Poincaré series. We also express the Fourier coefficients of Eisenstein series for mixed automorphic forms in terms of Jacquet integrals.

articleTitle: Bitangencies on Surfaces in Four Dimensions
abstract: We derive a formula relating the number of bitangencies, the number of double points and the normal Euler number of a generic closed surface in four‐dimensional Euclidean space. We give a geometric interpretation of the sign of a bitangency, and also we give a geometric interpretation of the correction term (the diagonal contribution) in the formula.

articleTitle: Two‐Dimensional Measured Laminations of Positive Euler Characteristic
abstract: The sphere lemma of A. Connes says that a compact oriented, 2‐dimensional measured lamination of positive Euler characteristic has many sphere leaves. The original proof of Connes uses non‐commutative geometry. We give a new proof, using branched surface methods borrowed from 3‐manifold theory, and some measure theory imported via Rochlin's lemma.

articleTitle: An Analogue of Peetre's Theorem in Non‐Commutative Topology
abstract: A linear mapping ∇: E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> → E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> between non‐commutative vector bundles E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> over a C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>‐algebra A is said to be local if, for all a, b ∈ A, ξ ∈ E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, aξ = ξb = 0 implies that a(∇ξ)b = 0. We show that a bounded linear mapping ∇ is local if and only if there is a derivation δ: A → L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</inf>(E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) such that ∇(aξ) = (δa)ξ + a∇ξ for all a ∈ A, ξ ∈ E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>.For a not necessarily bounded, linear mapping ∇: A → A on a unital C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>‐algebra A, a variant of locality implies the existence of a derivation δ: A → A and an element h ∈ A such that ∇(x) = δ(x) + hx, x ∈ A.

articleTitle: Spaces of Holomorphic Maps with Bounded Multiplicity
abstract: Let Hol<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> (S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, CP<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n−1</sup>) be the space consisting of all basepoint preserving holomorphic maps f : S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> → CP<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n−1</sup> of degree d. Then it is homeomorphic to the n‐tuples (p<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>(z), …, p<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>(z)) ∈ C[z]<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> of monic polynomials of degree d with no common root. Segal proved that it is a finite‐dimensional model of Ω<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> CP<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n−1</sup>. In this paper, we consider a certain subspace of it defined using the concept of multiplicity of roots, and we prove that it is also a finite‐dimensional model of certain double loop space.

articleTitle: Derivations on Banach–Jordan Pairs
Rational Minimal Surfaces
abstract: In this paper we investigate rational minimal surfaces—a special class of umbilic‐free minimal surfaces with finite total curvature and Enneper type ends. We define an iteration for Gauss maps and show that it can be used to produce infinitely many families of rational functions that yield rational minimal surfaces—the Schwarzian derivative plays an important role in the proof. We also investigate a relationship between the transformation used in the iteration and the Darboux–Bäcklund transformation for the Korteweg–de Vries equation.

articleTitle: Estimates for absolutely summing norms of polynomials and multilinear maps
abstract: We obtain lower bounds for the usual norms and the absolutely summing norms of polynomials and multilinear mappings from l<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> or c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> to a Banach space.Our estimates unify and extend the work of several previous authors who have worked with scalar‐valued mappings.

articleTitle: Spaces of particles on manifolds and generalized poincaré dualities
abstract: In this paper, we use a ‘local to global’ scanning process based on a construction of Segal to unify and generalize interesting results throughout the literature relating multi‐configuration spaces to mapping spaces.

articleTitle: Metrical Theorems on the Integer Parts of Real Sequences
abstract: Earlier work of the author on prime values of [10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>α] for almost all α > 0 is complemented by the construction of ‘prime‐like’ sets A for which [10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>α] ∈ A has only finitely many solutions for almost all α.

articleTitle: The Degree of the Divisor of Jumping Rational Curves
abstract: For a semistable reflexive sheaf E of rank r and c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> = a on P<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> and an integer d such that r|ad, we give sufficient conditions so that the restriction of E on a generic rational curve of degree d is balanced, that is, a twist of the trivial bundle (for instance, if E has balanced restriction on a generic line, or r = 2 or E is an exterior power of the tangent bundle). Assuming this, we give a formula for the ‘virtual degree’, interpreted enumeratively, of the (codimension‐1) locus of rational curves of degree d on which the restriction of E is not balanced, generalizing a classical formula due to Barth for the degree of the divisor of jumping lines of a semistable rank‐2 bundle. This amounts to computing a certain determinant line bundle associated to E on a parameter space for rational curves, and is closely related to the ‘quantum K‐theory’ of projective space.

articleTitle: On compressing discs of torus knots
abstract: We prove that every compressing disc of a (2n+1,2) ‐torus knot has at least 2n negative intersections with the knot; this implies that, in the language of [2], the natural framing is −2n. The proof uses an explicit and elementary simplification procedure for compressing discs.

articleTitle: Atomic decomposition of real JBW‐triples
abstract: We study the natural partial ordering in the set of all tripotents of a real JB*‐triple. We prove some characterizations of real‐minimal tripotents and an atomic deocmpostion theorem for real JBW*‐triples is given.

articleTitle: The exceptional set in Roth's theorem concerning a cube and three cubes of primes
abstract: It is proved that, with at most O (N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> 169/170</sup>) exceptions, all positive integers up to N are the sum of a cube and three cubes of primes. This improves a classical result of Roth.

articleTitle: Additive Representation in Thin Sequences, IV: Lower Bound Methods
abstract: We describe a method for establishing that values from a fixed polynomial sequence are represented frequently by some prescribed sum of powers of natural numbers. As an illustration of this method, we show that for at least X<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">129/136</sup> of the integers n with 1 ≤ n ≤ X, a fixed quadratic polynomial φ(n) may be written as the sum of five cubes of positive integers. A similar result is established for the sum of a square and three cubes of positive integers.

articleTitle: On Some Dyadic Properties of Curves
abstract: Using the dyadic parametrization of certain non‐rectifiable curves we introduce certain quantities which are discrete analogues of the second difference. These quantities can be viewed as random variables and this enables us to apply theorems from probability theory. This procedure enables us to construct in a routine manner non‐rectifiable curves having various differentiability properties.

articleTitle: Two‐Bridge Knots with Property Q
abstract: A knot k in S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> has property Q if there is a closed surface S in S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> containing k such that k is imprimitive in H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>A and H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>B where A and B are the closures of the components ofS<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> – S. If, in addition, lk(k, k<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>) ≠ 0, where k<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> is contained in S and is parallel to k, then k has property Q<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>. We determine the 2‐bridge knots K(β/α) that have property Q in terms of a continued fraction expansion of α/β. We also prove that the following conditions are equivalent: (i) K(β/α) has property Q; (ii) K(β/α) has property Q<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>; (iii) There is an epimorphism from the group of K(β/α) onto a free product; (iv) There is an epimorphism from the group of K(β/α) onto Z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> * Z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf>.

articleTitle: Standard Einstein Solvmanifolds as Critical Points
abstract: The aim of this note is to characterize the rank‐one Einstein solvmanifolds of a given dimension as the critical points of the modified scalar curvature functional. We vary Lie algebra brackets on a fixed inner product space instead of left invariant metrics on a given Lie group.

articleTitle: Midpoint Locally Uniform Rotundity and a Decomposition Method for Renorming
